agree.reason: The match and the $575 child-year give a lapsed donor a concrete reason to return, but someone still upset about Eastside gets only 'we heard you', with nothing on why the branch closed or what has changed, so they may not give.

honest.reason: It drops the brief's unsupportable promise that every child is guaranteed a place and says plainly 'We won't reach all 61 this month'; every figure it uses comes from the brief.

works_the_facts.reason: Doubling the $85 average gift and showing that $575 matched funds a full child-year are good derivations, but it never works out that a fully used match ($30,000) funds about 26 of the 61 children, or that clearing the whole list needs $70,150.

right_comparison.reason: It never spells out what happens if the reader doesn't give (children stay on the list, and any unused match money is lost), and it doesn't use last year's 9 gifts and $1,240 to show how far below this need ordinary giving falls.

qualification.reason: The hedge is real and checkable: not all 61 will be reached, the December 31 deadline and $15,000 cap are named, and a January report on the number placed is promised, though it gives no target number to judge that report against.

objections.reason: It raises the Eastside closure directly and doesn't avoid it, but the reply is only acknowledgment, with no reason for the closure and no sign that Eastside families are served now, so the resisting reader's grievance is named but not answered.

fit.reason: It is a year-end appeal email of roughly 235 words, under the 250 limit, signed by the executive director, with a clear subject line, a call to action and a P.S.
